note.text:
Weather words:
• Rain: a drizzle (light rain), a shower (short rain), a downpour (very heavy rain), a thunderstorm (rain with thunder and lightning).
• Wind: a breeze (a gentle wind), a gale (a very strong wind), the harmattan (a dry, dusty wind).
• Sky: clear, cloudy, overcast (completely grey), foggy or misty (you cannot see far).
• Temperature: scorching (very hot), warm, cool, chilly (a little cold).
• Humid means the air is warm and wet. A drought is a long time with no rain. A flood is when water covers dry land.
Nouns and adjectives: sun → sunny, cloud → cloudy, rain → rainy, wind → windy, fog → foggy, storm → stormy.

worked_example.problem: Make the weather adjectives from {a}, {b} and {c}, and use one in a sentence.
steps: Add -y. A short word ending in one vowel + one consonant doubles it: {a} → sunny, {b} → foggy.
Sentence: It was so foggy on the mountain that we could not see the road.

cards.idea: Rain can be light (a drizzle), short (a shower), very heavy (a downpour) or stormy (a thunderstorm).
example: A drizzle hardly wets your clothes.
In a downpour, the gutters overflow.

cards.idea: Add -y to a weather noun to make an adjective: rain → rainy. Double a final consonant after one short vowel: sun → sunny.

pick.s: It is very ___ today; take your hat.
We could not see the road: it was ___.

e: Do not double the d: cloudy.

pick.s: It is ___; hold on to your umbrella.
e: Do not double the d: windy.

pick.s: The night was ___, with thunder and lightning.
e: Do not double the m: stormy.

cards.idea: Humid means warm and wet air. A drought is a long time with no rain; a flood is water over dry land.
example: After the downpour there was a flood in the street.

pick.s: There was no rain for six months; the ___ killed the maize.
e: A flood is too much water.

pick.s: It's only a ___; you don't need an umbrella.
e: A downpour is very heavy rain.

pick.s: A cool ___ came from the sea in the evening.
e: A drought is a time with no rain.

questions.prompt: One sentence uses a weather word wrongly. Which one?

right.text: A gentle breeze cooled the room.
It was foggy on the mountain.

wrong.text: The drizzle was so heavy that the bridge broke.
wrong.explain: A drizzle is very light rain; heavy rain is a downpour.

wrong.text: We had a flood because it did not rain for months.
wrong.explain: No rain for months is a drought.

wrong.text: It is scorching, so wear a warm sweater.
